results.title: Anisotropy of the quaternion norm form reduces to a ternary form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The quaternary norm form `x₀² - a·x₁² - b·x₂² + a·b·x₃²` of the quaternion algebra `ℍ[K, a, b]` is anisotropic if and only if the ternary form `z² - a·x² - b·y²` is. This equivalence also holds when either parameter is zero; both forms are then isotropic.

results.title: Quaternion algebras with isotropic norm form split
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the norm form of a quaternion algebra over a field of characteristic not two is isotropic, then the algebra splits: it is isomorphic to the `2 × 2` matrix algebra.

results.title: Torsion-freeness of abelianized Cartesian powers of free groups (Kourovka 13.18)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, posed by A. M. Gaglione and D. Spellman, that for every integer $n \ge 2$ the abelianization of the unrestricted (Cartesian) product $F_n^{\mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ is torsion-free: none of its nontrivial elements has finite order.

results.title: Abelianized Cartesian powers of free groups can have torsion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For some integer $n \ge 2$, the abelianization of the unrestricted (Cartesian) product $F_n^{\mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains a nontrivial element of finite order. That is, the torsion-freeness asked for in Kourovka Problem 13.18 fails.

results.title: Zalesskiĭ's problem on eigenvalues of elements of prime order (Kourovka 11.35)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every $n$, every finite subgroup $H$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and every $h \in H$ of prime order $p$ that lies in no abelian normal subgroup of $H$, the element $h$ has at least $(p - 1)/2$ distinct eigenvalues, that is, $p - 1 \le 2k$ where $k$ is the number of distinct roots of the characteristic polynomial of $h$.

results.title: Robinson's theorem on eigenvalues of elements of prime order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, if $H$ is a finite subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $h \in H$ has prime order $p$ and lies in no abelian normal subgroup of $H$, then $h$ has at least $(p - 1)/2$ distinct eigenvalues, that is, $p - 1 \le 2k$ where $k$ is the number of distinct roots of the characteristic polynomial of $h$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 11.35 (A. E. Zalesskiĭ) in the affirmative.

results.title: Balancing numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The balancing numbers are the integers $B_n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ defined by $B_0 = 0$, $B_1 = 1$ and $B_{n+2} = 6 B_{n+1} - B_n$ for all $n$.

results.title: Differences of two repdigits
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a difference of two repdigits if there are repdigits $a$ and $b$ with $a = n + b$, that is, $n = a - b$.

results.title: Linear fractional pole series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $c$, this is the power series $F_{a,c}(u)$ of $\frac{cu}{a - cu}$: it is $\sum_{n \ge 1} (c/a)^n u^n$ if $a \neq 0$, the constant $-1$ if $a = 0$ and $c \neq 0$, and $0$ (a junk value) if $a = c = 0$. It is $u$ times the summand $\frac{c}{a - cu}$ of $G_g(u) = \frac{c}{a - cu} - \frac{d}{b - du}$ for the matrix $g$ with rows $(a, b)$ and $(c, d)$.

results.title: The linear fractional pole series solves its defining equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $a$ and $c$, the linear fractional pole series $F_{a,c}(u)$, the power series of $\frac{cu}{a - cu}$, satisfies $(a - cu) \cdot F_{a,c}(u) = cu$ in $\mathbb{R}[[u]]$.

results.title: Landen form series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $a, b, c, d$, viewed as the matrix $g$ with rows $(a, b)$ and $(c, d)$, this is the power series $u \cdot G_g(u) = \frac{cu}{a - cu} - \frac{du}{b - du} \in \mathbb{R}[[u]]$, where $G_g(t) = \frac{c}{a - ct} - \frac{d}{b - dt}$. Here the power series of $\frac{cu}{a - cu}$ is $\sum_{n \ge 1} (c/a)^n u^n$ if $a \neq 0$, the constant $-1$ if $a = 0$ and $c \neq 0$, and $0$ if $a = c = 0$; likewise…

results.title: Landen form series of the identity matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the identity matrix $g$, with rows $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$, the Landen form series $u \cdot G_g(u)$ is the constant power series $1$ in $\mathbb{R}[[u]]$; that is, $G_g(t) = 1/t$.

results.title: Formal integral against $du/u$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real power series $h$, this is the power series $\int_0^z h(u)\,du/u$ computed coefficientwise: for $n \ge 1$ its coefficient of $z^n$ is the coefficient of $u^n$ in $h$ divided by $n$, and its constant coefficient is $0$. The constant coefficient of $h$ is ignored, so this is the termwise integral only when $h$ has zero constant term.

results.title: The formal integral against $du/u$ is a right inverse of $z \, d/dz$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h \in \mathbb{R}[[z]]$ be a power series with zero constant term, and let $I(h) = \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{[z^n] h}{n} z^n$ be its formal integral $\int_0^z h(u) \, du / u$, where $[z^n] h$ is the coefficient of $z^n$ in $h$. Then $I(h)$ has zero constant term and $z \, \frac{d}{dz} I(h) = h$.

results.title: Landen data

results.title: The transformation of Landen data is an involution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Landen data $g = (g_0, g_1, \dots, g_s)$ with $g_0 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ c_0 & d_0 \end{pmatrix}$, let $\tilde g$ be the transformed data, given by $\tilde g_i = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ c_0 - d_0 & -1 \end{pmatrix} g_i$ for $0 \le i \le s$. Then the transformed data of $\tilde g$ is $g$ itself: $\tilde{\tilde g} = g$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g = (g_0, g_1, \dots, g_s)$ be Landen data, where $g_0$ has rows $(1, -1)$ and $(c_0, d_0)$, and let $\beta, \gamma \in \mathbb{R}^s$. results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Landen exponential variable

results.title: Every positive integer is a practical number plus a triangular number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$ there are a practical number $q$ and a natural number $k$ with $n = q + k(k+1)/2$; the case $k = 0$, where the triangular number is $0$, is allowed.

results.title: Large integers as a practical number plus two polygonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s > 3$ be a natural number and, for a natural number $x$, let $P_s(x) = (s-2)\binom{x}{2} + x$ be the $x$-th $s$-gonal number, so that $P_s(0) = 0$. There is a natural number $N$ such that every natural number $n > N$ can be written as $n = q + P_s(x) + P_s(y)$ with $q$ a practical number and $x, y$ natural numbers.

results.title: Square roots modulo powers of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $m > 0$ and $n > 0$ there is a natural number $x$ with $1 \le x \le 2^m - 1$ and $x^2 \equiv 8n + 1 \pmod{2^{m+2}}$.

results.title: Products of a practical number with small factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a practical number and let $\sigma(m)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of $m$. Then for every natural number $n$ with $1 \le n \le \sigma(m) + 1$, the product $mn$ is a practical number.

results.title: Odd squares and triangular numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every odd natural number $x$, the number $(x^2 - 1)/8$ is a triangular number: there is a natural number $k$ with $(x^2 - 1)/8 = p_3(k)$, where $p_3(k) = k(k+1)/2$ is the $k$-th $3$-gonal number.

results.title: Sums of two polygonal numbers modulo an odd prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $s > 3$ and a natural number $x$, let $P_s(x) = (s-2)\binom{x}{2} + x$ be the $x$-th $s$-gonal number. For every odd prime $p$ and every natural number $n > 0$ there are natural numbers $x, y > 0$ with $P_s(x) + P_s(y) \equiv n \pmod{p}$.

results.title: Parity of sums of two polygonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $s > 3$ and a natural number $x$, let $P_s(x) = (s-2)\binom{x}{2} + x$ be the $x$-th $s$-gonal number. For every natural number $n > 0$ there are natural numbers $x, y > 0$ such that $P_s(x_1) + P_s(y_1) \equiv n \pmod{2}$ for all natural numbers $x_1, y_1 > 0$ with $x_1 \equiv x \pmod{4}$ and $y_1 \equiv y \pmod{4}$.

results.title: Sums of two squares modulo prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$. For all natural numbers $n > 0$ and $k > 0$ there are natural numbers $x, y > 0$ with $x^2 + y^2 \equiv n \pmod{p^k}$ and $p \nmid y$.

results.title: Sums of two polygonal numbers modulo prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $s > 3$ and a natural number $x$, let $P_s(x) = (s-2)\binom{x}{2} + x$ be the $x$-th $s$-gonal number. There is a prime $p$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$ and $p \nmid s - 2$ such that for all natural numbers $k > 0$ and $n > 0$ there are natural numbers $x, y > 0$ with $P_s(x) + P_s(y) \equiv n \pmod{p^k}$.

results.title: Quadratic upper bound for polygonal numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $s > 3$ and a natural number $x$, let $P_s(x) = (s-2)\binom{x}{2} + x$ be the $x$-th $s$-gonal number. For every natural number $c$ there is a natural number $A$ such that $2 P_s(2cx) \le A x^2$ for every natural number $x \ge 1$.

results.title: Practical numbers divisible by neither 3 nor 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $q$ is a practical number that is divisible by neither $3$ nor $4$, then $q = 1$ or $q = 2$.

results.title: Scheffé's lemma on the real line
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable and let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integrable real functions $f_n$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that $f_n(x) \to f(x)$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$. If $\int_{\mathbb{R}} |f_n| \to \int_{\mathbb{R}} |f|$ as $n \to \infty$, then $\int_{\mathbb{R}} |f_n - f| \to 0$.

results.title: Chi-square distribution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of freedom is the gamma law on $\mathbb{R}$ with shape $p/2$ and rate $1/2$ (equivalently, scale $2$): the measure with density $x \mapsto \frac{(1/2)^{p/2}}{\Gamma(p/2)} x^{p/2 - 1} e^{-x/2}$ for $x > 0$ and $0$ for $x < 0$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

results.title: Moment generating function of the square of a standard normal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$). For every real $t$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x^2} \, d\gamma(x) = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

results.title: Exponential moments of the square of a standard normal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$). For every real $t < 1/2$, the function $x \mapsto e^{t x^2}$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma$.

results.title: Exponential moments of the law of the square of a standard normal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$) and let $\nu$ be its image under $x \mapsto x^2$. For every real $t < 1/2$, the function $y \mapsto e^{t y}$ is integrable with respect to $\nu$.

results.title: Moment generating function of the law of the square of a standard normal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$) and let $\nu$ be its image under $x \mapsto x^2$. For every real $t$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t y} \, d\nu(y) = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

results.title: Moment generating function of the gamma law with shape and rate one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be the gamma law on $\mathbb{R}$ with shape $1/2$ and rate $1/2$. For every real $t < 1/2$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x} \, d\mu(x) = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

results.title: Moment generating function of the chi-square distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $\chi^2_p$ be the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of freedom. For every real $t < 1/2$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x} \, d\chi^2_p(x) = \left(\frac{1/2}{1/2 - t}\right)^{p/2}$.

results.title: Exponential moments of the chi-square distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $\chi^2_p$ be the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of freedom. For every real $t < 1/2$, the function $x \mapsto e^{t x}$ is integrable with respect to $\chi^2_p$.

results.title: Global second-order bound for the imaginary exponential
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $u$, $|e^{iu} - 1 - iu| \le u^2$, with no restriction on the size of $u$.

results.title: Second-order Taylor bound for the characteristic function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space with $X^2$ integrable, and let $\varphi_X$ be the characteristic function of the law of $X$. Then for every real $t$, $|\varphi_X(t) - 1 - it\,\mathbb{E}[X]| \le t^2 \, \mathbb{E}[X^2]$.

results.title: First-order Taylor bound for the characteristic function

results.title: Characteristic-function second-order bound

results.title: Erdős Problem 751
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that both of the following hold: (i) for every natural number $k$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$; (ii) for all natural numbers $k$ and $g$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ and girth at least $g$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 751 is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that both of the following hold: (i) for every natural number $k$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$; (ii) for all natural numbers $k$ and $g$ there is a simple graph $G$ with chromatic number $4$ and girth at least $g$ in which any two distinct cycle lengths of $G$ differ by at least $k$.

results.title: Odd cycle lengths and infinite chromatic number (Erdős Problem 57)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on an arbitrary vertex set that has no proper colouring with finitely many colours. Then the family $(1/\ell)$, indexed by the odd cycle lengths $\ell$ of $G$ (the odd numbers $\ell$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$), is not summable; that is, $\sum_\ell 1/\ell = \infty$.

results.title: Resolution of the Erdős–Hajnal odd cycle problem (Liu–Montgomery)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on an arbitrary vertex set that has no proper colouring with finitely many colours. Then the family $(1/\ell)$, indexed by the odd cycle lengths $\ell$ of $G$ (the odd numbers $\ell$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$), is not summable; that is, $\sum_\ell 1/\ell = \infty$.

results.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 63
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every simple graph $G$ with infinite chromatic number has cycles of length $2^n$ for infinitely many $n$: for every natural number $N$ there is some $n \ge N$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $2^n$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 63 (Liu–Montgomery)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every simple graph $G$ with infinite chromatic number has cycles of length $2^n$ for infinitely many $n$: for every natural number $N$ there is some $n \ge N$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $2^n$.

results.title: Andrásfai graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Andrásfai graph is the Cayley graph of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/(3k+2)\mathbb{Z}$ whose connection set $C$ consists of the residues whose representative in $\{0, 1, \dots, 3k+1\}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $3$: two distinct residues $x$ and $y$ are adjacent when $y - x \in C$ or $x - y \in C$.

results.title: Cayley digraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with a binary operation written as multiplication, and let $C \subseteq G$. The *Cayley digraph* $X(G, C)$ is the directed graph whose vertices are the elements of $G$, with an arc $u \to v$ exactly when $v = uc$ for some $c \in C$.

results.title: Cayley's formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the complete graph on $n$ vertices has exactly $n^{n-2}$ spanning trees.

results.title: Coxeter graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Coxeter graph is the simple graph whose $28$ vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and whose edges are the following: for each $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, the vertices $(i, j)$ and $(i, j')$ are adjacent when $j - j' = i$ or $j' - j = i$ in $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and for each $j$ the vertex $(0, j)$ is adjacent to $(1, j)$, $(2, j)$ and $(3, j)$. results.title: Edge-transposition graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a set of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$, typically a set of transpositions in the symmetric group $S_n$. The edge-transposition graph of $T$ is the simple graph with vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which two distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if the transposition swapping $i$ and $j$ belongs to $T$.

results.title: Frucht's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a finite simple graph.

results.title: Moore graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $d$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is a Moore graph of diameter $d$ when $G$ has diameter $d$ and girth $2d + 1$.

results.title: Petersen graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Petersen graph is the generalized Johnson graph $J(5,2,0)$: its vertices are the $2$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$, and two of them are adjacent exactly when they are disjoint.

results.title: Vertex-transitive graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A graph is vertex-transitive when its automorphism group acts transitively on vertices.

results.title: Malécot's identity-by-descent model
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Malécot's identity-by-descent model at one biallelic locus, at the level of second moments. The individuals are `ι`; individual `i` carries the gene copies `(i, 0)` (paternal) and `(i, 1)` (maternal), and `allele c ∈ {0, 1}` indicates the reference allele on copy `c`. results.title: Genotype of an individual at a biallelic locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genotype (reference-allele count) `x_i ∈ {0, 1, 2}` of individual `i`.

results.title: Kinship coefficient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The kinship coefficient `φ_ij`: the probability that a copy drawn at random from `i` and a copy drawn at random from `j` are identical by descent.

results.title: Inbreeding coefficient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient `F_i`: the probability that the two copies of `i` are identical by descent.

results.title: Genetic relationship matrix entry
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genetic relationship matrix entry of Yang et al. (2010) at one locus, `A_ij = (x_i - 2p)(x_j - 2p) / (2p(1 - p))`.

results.title: GCTA diagonal relationship estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The diagonal estimator of GCTA (Yang et al. 2011) at one locus, `A_ii = 1 + (x_i² - (1 + 2p) x_i + 2p²) / (2p(1 - p))`.

results.title: Integrability of allele indicators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The allele indicators are integrable.

results.title: Integrability of products of allele indicators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Products of allele indicators are integrable.

results.title: A gene copy is identical by descent with itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A gene copy is identical by descent with itself: `ibd c c = 1`.

results.title: Symmetry of identity by descent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Identity by descent is symmetric.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Symmetry of kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kinship is symmetric.

results.title: Integrability of genotypes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Genotypes are integrable.

results.title: Integrability of products of genotypes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Products of genotypes are integrable.

results.title: Expected genotype equals $2p$
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Second moment of genotypes in terms of kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `𝔼[x_i x_j] = 4p² + 4p(1 - p) φ_ij`.

results.title: The genetic relationship covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The genetic relationship covariance (Yang et al. 2010): `𝔼[(x_i - 2p)(x_j - 2p)] = 2p(1 - p) · 2 φ_ij`.

results.title: The GRM is unbiased for twice the kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The GRM is unbiased for twice the kinship (Yang et al. 2010): `𝔼[A_ij] = 2 φ_ij`, for every pair `i, j` (including `i = j`, where `2 φ_ii = 1 + F_i`).

results.title: Diagonal GRM entry is unbiased for $1 + F_i$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The diagonal GRM entry is unbiased for `1 + F_i`: `𝔼[A_ii] = 1 + F_i`.

results.title: The KING moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The KING moment (Manichaikul et al. 2010), general form: `𝔼[(x_i - x_j)²] = 2p(1 - p)(1 + F_i) + 2p(1 - p)(1 + F_j) - 8p(1 - p) φ_ij`.

results.title: The KING moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The KING moment (Manichaikul et al. 2010) for two non-inbred individuals: `𝔼[(x_i - x_j)²] = 4p(1 - p)(1 - 2φ_ij)`.

results.title: The GCTA diagonal estimator is unbiased for `1 + F_i`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The GCTA diagonal estimator is unbiased for `1 + F_i` (Yang et al. 2011): `𝔼[1 + (x_i² - (1 + 2p) x_i + 2p²) / (2p(1 - p))] = 1 + F_i`.
